# Adoption & Operator Experience Requirements Checklist: Jisr MCP Server

**Purpose**: Validate that installation, configuration, and operator-facing *requirements* are specific enough to build and measure — with particular attention to per-client installation for Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor
**Created**: 2026-08-29
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Per-Client Installation Requirements

- [ ] CHK001 Are installation requirements specified separately for **Claude Code**, naming the configuration mechanism and file it uses? [Gap, Spec §FR-004]
- [ ] CHK002 Are installation requirements specified separately for **Codex**, whose MCP configuration format differs from the JSON used by other clients? [Gap, Spec §FR-004]
- [ ] CHK003 Are installation requirements specified separately for **Cursor**, including whether project-scoped and user-scoped installation are both supported? [Gap, Spec §FR-004]
- [ ] CHK004 Does the spec require that each client's configuration block be exact and runnable, rather than illustrative? [Clarity, Spec §FR-004]
- [ ] CHK005 Are requirements defined for how credentials are supplied per client, given some clients pass environment variables and others do not? [Gap, Coverage]
- [ ] CHK006 Is it specified whether both scoped installation modes — per-project and per-user — must be documented where a client supports both? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-004]
- [ ] CHK007 Are requirements defined for keeping per-client instructions accurate as those clients change their configuration formats? [Gap, Maintenance]
- [ ] CHK008 Is "a ChatGPT/Codex-family client" resolved to a specific named client, rather than a family? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-003]
- [ ] CHK009 Are requirements specified for which of the five named clients must support the v2 adapter versus the v1 adapter? [Gap, research R3]

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK010 Is the published package name and registry scope specified, given the quickstart currently carries a placeholder? [Gap, quickstart.md]
- [ ] CHK011 Are requirements defined for detecting and reporting an unsupported Node version at startup? [Gap, Spec §FR-006]
- [ ] CHK012 Is configuration precedence specified when the same setting arrives from more than one source? [Gap, Coverage]
- [ ] CHK013 Are requirements defined for operation behind an HTTP proxy or in a restricted-egress network? [Gap, Coverage]
- [ ] CHK014 Is Windows support required, or is cross-platform support asserted in the plan without a corresponding requirement? [Gap, Plan §Technical Context]
- [ ] CHK015 Are requirements defined for how an adopter upgrades, and what compatibility they may assume across versions? [Gap, Spec §FR-044]
- [ ] CHK016 Are requirements specified for the language of operator-facing messages, given the product targets Arabic-speaking organizations? [Gap]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK017 Does SC-001 define the measurement protocol for "under 10 minutes" — starting point, hardware, network, and whether credential provisioning counts? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001]
- [ ] CHK018 Is "without reading source code" observable, or a statement of intent? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001]
- [ ] CHK019 Is "actionable" defined for startup failure messages, beyond naming the setting? [Clarity, Spec §FR-006]
- [ ] CHK020 Is the required README content enumerated, or only its outcome described? [Clarity, Spec §FR-041]
- [ ] CHK021 Is "single documented command" precise about whether a package manager install step counts against it? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-001]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK022 Is the client list consistent between FR-003, SC-006, and the quickstart's validation scenario? [Consistency, Spec §FR-003]
- [ ] CHK023 Do the configuration variable names in the quickstart match those the spec implies for the finance opt-in? [Consistency, quickstart.md]
- [ ] CHK024 Is the two-credential posture consistently presented as recommended in one place and required in another? [Consistency, Spec §FR-023b, quickstart.md]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK025 Is SC-005 ("agent can determine the reason in 100% of unavailability cases") bounded by an enumerated set of unavailability causes? [Measurability, Spec §SC-005]
- [ ] CHK026 Does SC-010 define what counts as a "distinct Jisr domain" and what "uninterrupted session" means? [Clarity, Spec §SC-010]
- [ ] CHK027 Are acceptance criteria defined for the per-client installation instructions themselves, or only for the server they configure? [Gap, Spec §FR-004]

## Scenario & Edge Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK028 Are requirements defined for an adopter whose organization is locally hosted rather than AWS-hosted, including how they determine which? [Coverage, Spec §FR-006]
- [ ] CHK029 Are requirements specified for the case where the API secret — shown once by Jisr — was not captured? [Edge Case, Gap]
- [ ] CHK030 Are requirements defined for an adopter connecting a key with no permissions at all? [Edge Case, Coverage]
- [ ] CHK031 Are requirements defined for a client that cannot display a tool's human-readable summary? [Coverage, Gap]
- [ ] CHK032 Are requirements specified for diagnosing a failed connection without exposing credentials in the diagnostic output? [Coverage, Spec §FR-013]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [ ] CHK033 Is the assumption stated that adopters can obtain Jisr API credentials themselves, and the consequence if they cannot? [Assumption, Spec §Dependencies]
- [ ] CHK034 Is the assumption recorded that the five named clients will continue to support the protocol versions the server implements? [Assumption, Gap]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- CHK001–CHK009 were added at explicit request. FR-004 currently requires per-client configuration blocks without naming the clients' differing mechanisms — Codex in particular does not use the same configuration format as the others, so one generic block cannot satisfy the requirement as written
